To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) deep language models can help to alleviate the problem of annotation paucity for semantic role labeling, (2) they can improve the performance for both "known" predicates (present in the training set) and "unknown" ones (not in the training set), and (3) they can help to improve the performance on both known and unknown predicates even in the case of small training sets.

(1) the pipeline for semantic role labeling of Russian texts is implemented and evaluated; (2) the neural network models for semantic role labeling can be trained with embeddings generated by deep language models; (3) the models can be trained for "known" and for "unknown" predicate classes.

the use of deep pretrained language models for semantic role labeling in general and argument classification in particular is promising.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of deep pretrained language models for semantic role labeling is a viable alternative to classical shallow embeddings and can be a solution to the problem of annotation sparsity.

we build a full semantic role labelling pipeline and show that it is feasible to train neural network models with deep pretrained language models to perform semantic role labelling for both "known" predicates and "unknown" ones.

we build the first full semantic role labelling pipeline for Russian texts, show that the pipeline can work with "unknown" predicates and provide the first evidence that embeddings generated by pretrained language models can improve argument classification of "known" as well as "unknown" predicates.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of pretrained embeddings for "unknown" predicate classification can be a viable solution for the problem of annotation sparsity in the semantic role labeling task.
the combination of deep pretrained language models and supervised learning is a promising approach to semantic role labelling for Russian.
deep pretrained language models can be effectively used to improve semantic role labelling even when the training data is scarce.
